- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and underperform after spikes; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for positive sentiment trends.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.00) or neutral; increase forecast by 3–7% for negative sentiment to compensate for market underreaction.
- Lagging forecasts often overshoot early in the horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply a 1–2% downward correction for forecasts 1–3 days ahead if sentiment is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–3% per day.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers a 5–10% upward adjustment in forecast to capture momentum shift.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, reduce by 2–4% if sentiment is consistently positive over last 7 days; increase by 2–4% if sentiment is consistently negative.
